svg.title: Bec256's fixed division of bit positions
svg.desc: The whole block covers positions zero through 255 and has supplied population p. Its left half covers zero through 127 with encoded count q; its right half covers 128 through 255 with inferred count p minus q. Repeating the same division in both halves produces four regions of 64 positions, eight of 32, sixteen of 16 and thirty-two byte-sized leaves of eight positions. The tree boundaries are fixed. The split fields recover every byte's population; byte ranks then select its pattern.

g.text: One fixed tree, with counts recovered from parent to child
Horizontal position follows bit index throughout · lower positions are always on the left
Repeat in each half, using that region's population as p.
Leaf labels are plain byte indices 0..31; their populations are now known.
Next: a rank selects the exact bit pattern within each byte.
